votes.refutation: I first checked whether the PR row lock, stale-clock check, delivery id, or supersession guards collapse the two triggers. The lock serializes them but still permits two sequential rows; equal timestamps pass, and only the webhook has a delivery id. The sandbox/pre-post superseded guards (activities.py:383-389,416-429,700-713) do prevent stale publication and can avoid spending on a first run still queued, so the claim does not establish an unsafe approval race. They cannot undo a sandbox already running when the later duplicate arrives. The retained issue is concrete duplicate expensive work and review delay for the normal receiver-plus-synchronize ordering, with narrow timing impact, hence should_fix. Any fix must preserve legitimate same-head base-retarget or explicit re-review behavior.

The feared approval/comment correctness race is substantially refuted: activities.py:387-429 avoids provisioning superseded work, :700-713 rechecks status before posting, and :751-798 conditionally finalizes and dismisses orphan approvals; tests/test_integration.py:815 onward exercises late supersession. Same-head re-review is deliberately required for reopen/base/context changes, so a blanket same-head uniqueness constraint would be wrong. The surviving synchronize overlap is avoidable duplicate work, a minor issue (consider), not a proved unsafe approval.

votes.evidence: The initial receiver task fetches the current GitHub head and deduplicates against it at products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1159,1202-1221, then creates a run with delivery_id=None at 1223-1229. The synchronize path only deduplicates the delivery ID (994-1008), permits equal snapshot timestamps (1010-1014), and unconditionally supersedes active runs and creates another at 1054-1064. If an initial delivery or refire fetches head B before the delayed synchronize delivery for B, that delivery cannot match the receiver's null delivery ID and replaces its same-head run. Once the first run has passed temporal/activities.py:421-429 and created its sandbox at 466, this does duplicate review work; a completed first run also does not prevent the second run. Non-internal manual Inbox implementations are a real source of receiver and webhook triggers (frontend/src/scenes/inbox/inboxTaskKickoffLogic.ts:80-96).
votes.refutation: I checked timestamp ordering, locking, delivery-ID deduplication, and final posting guards. An older synchronize snapshot is correctly rejected, but equal timestamps explicitly proceed. The parent row lock serializes the two creations; it does not make the webhook inspect the existing head. Supersession guards prevent the first run from publishing after it observes cancellation (activities.py:666-672,700-713), so an unsafe-approval race is not needed to retain the claim. The proven defect is duplicate sandbox review/cancellation for one synchronize head. Any fix must still permit explicit same-head base-retarget re-review (tasks.py:832-835), rather than universally suppressing all same-head events.
